reason: 'Inflorescence 1-12-flowered' is a flower count per inflorescence; bearer flower in container inflorescence (PO_0009049), 1-12.
'leaf blade ... abaxially pubescent': the abaxial side of the leaf lamina is pubescent; substituting the abaxial surface is the right reading.
The peduncle is 'hairy like stem' and gets more black spreading hairs toward the raceme. Peduncle hairy is true; the gradient and colour are just not recorded.
Stipules adnate to the petiole, i.e. fused with it. The extent (about half its length) is not recorded, but the annotation is not false without it.
In FNA, 'Shrubs h × w dm' gives height × width. The width (1-)2-6(-9) dm converts to 20-60 cm, with extremes of 10 and 90 cm.
'Leaves pedately 9-11-foliolate' is a leaflet count per leaf, 9-11.
Sepals finely pilose to nearly glabrous: a continuum from pilose (FLOPO_0991048) to subglabrous (FLOPO_0991053), which correctly renders 'nearly glabrous'.

fix: In FOC, square brackets mark states found only outside China, and '?' marks doubt. '[?biennial]' does not assert biennial; skip it, or keep it only with an uncertain/outside-range qualifier.
reason: The flora asserts a [winter] annual. 'Biennial' is offered only as a doubtful, bracketed possibility, but the annotation states it as fact.
Spikelets 5-24-flowered: a floret count per spikelet (container PO_0009051).
'étamines 3' means 3 stamens.

fix: In Carex (Cyperaceae), 'utricle' means the perigynium, the sac around the achene, not the fruit. Map 'utricle(s)' to PO_0009044 when the taxon is Carex/Kobresia.
reason: The comparison 'longer than glume' is said of the Carex utricle (perigynium), not of the fruit inside it.

target: gland on the sporangium stalk (glands of the sporangium stalk)
fix: In 'X bearing <colour> <part>', the colour belongs to the borne part, not to X. The to_text 'orange glands' already swallows the part noun.
reason: The golden-to-orange colour is of the glands on the sporangium stalks, not of the sporangia. The 'approximately' qualifier also has no basis in the text.
9-12 lateral veins on each side of the midvein. The vein container and the each_side position together render this correctly.
'Leaves surpassing culm' means the leaves are longer than the culm (stem).

fix: In Asteraceae, floret counts ('disk florets N', 'ray florets N') are per head, never per flower. The container fallback to flower is wrong.
reason: The 4-8 disk florets are counted per head. Disk florets are not parts of a flower.
The leaf adaxial side ('above') has sparse stellate hairs and is glabrescent. Pilosity with the value glabrescent on the adaxial surface is true.
Phyllary apex acute or acuminate. Apex shape goes on the organ through the sensu-botany apex values, as alternatives.

target: height >= 100 cm, upper bound open (100-200+ cm)
fix: 'N+' (here '20+') marks an open upper bound (at least N, sometimes more). Record it as open-ended or as a max with a '+' flag, not as a closed maximum.
reason: '10-20+ dm' says plants can exceed 200 cm. A closed range of 100-200 cm wrongly caps the height.
Basal leaves 7-12 cm long; the basal context is kept.
Inflorescences many-flowered: flowers present in the inflorescence with the count word 'many'.
The lowest bract is shorter than the culm; the 'lower' context is kept.

fix: In mosses, 'perichaetial leaves' are a distinct kind of leaf around the archegonia. Keep 'perichaetial' as a whole/state slot (or a FLOPO anatomy class), not just 'outer leaf'.
reason: Only the outer perichaetial leaves are short-acuminate. 'Outer leaf' alone drops the perichaetium; the vegetative leaves are described separately.
Sepals 1-1.3 × 0.8-1 cm, so the length is 1-1.3 cm.
'umbels simple, many flowered': flowers present, 'many', in the inflorescence.

fix: A hyphenated colour compound 'X-Y' (brown-green) means Y tinged with X, not plain Y. Keep both hues (an X-ish Y value), or don't reduce it to the head colour.
reason: 'brown-green' was reduced to plain green, which loses the brown tinge.
Stipules brownish: brown, approximately.

fix: French 'internes'/'externes' after the noun (bractées involucrales internes) must fill the series-position slot, just as English 'inner'/'outer' does.
reason: The 3-4 longitudinal veins are said only of the inner involucral bracts; the outer ones are described differently earlier.
Leaves usually laminate: a leaf lamina is present, usually.
Rhizomes brownish.
'Annuals or biennials; (base not woody)': for these herbs, the whole plant not woody is true. Strictly the statement is about the plant base, but nothing is falsified.
